children: The Wella Company filed for an initial public offering, seeking to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "WELA." The hair and nail products company, which operates globally with brands like Wella Professionals, OPI, Clairol and ghd, has not yet disclosed a price range or share count. The filing states there has been no public market for its stock to date.

Wella is a global hair and nail beauty company operating in more than 100 countries. It sells professional and consumer products across two segments: Hair & Nail (color, care, styling and nail) and Beauty Tech (ghd styling tools). Its portfolio includes Wella Professionals (salon color and care), OPI (nail), Clairol and Wella/Koleston (at‑home color), Sebastian Professional and Nioxin (professional care), and ghd (heat- and air‑assisted hair devices). The company’s professional-first model leverages deep stylist relationships—supported by an in-house and partner manufacturing base—to seed innovation in salons and then expand winning products into consumer channels, including e-commerce, specialty beauty retail, FDM, club and premium retail.

Wella emphasizes science-led innovation with more than 300 scientists and over 1,200 granted and pending patents across six global R&D centers. Competitive advantages include a scaled brand portfolio with leading positions, a global direct sales organization focused on acquiring salons with color and expanding into care, and a robust supply chain that combines three owned manufacturing facilities with third-party partners. The Beauty Tech segment (ghd) complements the portfolio with premium devices such as stylers and dryers, protected by extensive IP and engineered for salon-grade performance without extreme heat damage.
: The global hair, nail, and hair appliances market is approximately $120 billion.

: Overall category expected to grow at ~5.6% CAGR from 2025 to 2029; beauty e-commerce grew at 11.9% CAGR from 2022 to 2025; premium hair care projected to grow at 5.4% CAGR; professional hair care grew 7% CAGR from 2022 to 2025.
: Wella Professionals holds the #1 global brand rank in salon hair color; OPI is the #1 premium retail nail brand globally.
: L’Oréal, Henkel, Kao, Unilever, Estée Lauder.
: Rising self‑care and wellness focus, premiumization, strong stylist influence, social/digital discovery, and omnichannel expansion.
: Serves over 250,000 salons and hundreds of thousands of stylists globally; direct relationships with ~65,000 salons through its DSO.
: Operates in 100+ countries with three owned factories (Germany, Mexico, Thailand).
: Americas, EMEA, and APAC; U.S. accounted for ~25–28% of recent segment revenues.
: Deep ties with professional salons; premium and mass retail partners; marketplaces including Amazon.

: 750+ sales representatives; 300 educators; ~4,700 new strategic salon doors added in FY26; 98% salon revenue retention and 88 NPS in FY26; e-commerce/marketplaces ~23% of net invoiced sales in FY26; supply chain team ~2,000; 27 Hair & Nail and 11 Beauty Tech distribution centers; fill rate ~97%; 46 Wella Studios and 60+ Training Centers; ~850,000 stylist education interactions annually across ~60,000 salons with 4.9/5 rating; ghd gross margin ~69%.
: Up 9.2% year over year (reported) from FY2025; up from $2.59B in FY2024
, Chief Executive Officer and Director - Former CEO of Lululemon; previously led Sephora Americas; earlier roles at Sears Canada and Loblaw.
, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer - Former CFO of Boston Beer Company; earlier leadership roles at Kraft Foods and Philip Morris.
, Chief Revenue Officer - Previously President, EMEA/APAC at Wella; senior leadership roles at L’Oréal and Coty.
, Chief Legal Officer - Former Chief Legal and Sustainability Officer at Capri Holdings; earlier at Paul, Weiss.
, Chief Marketing Officer - Former CEO of BH Cosmetics; 18+ years at L’Oréal across brands and regions.
, Chief Executive Officer, ghd - Over 20 years in beauty; senior roles at L’Oréal; leads ghd since 2018.
: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC; BofA Securities; KKR Capital Markets; J.P. Morgan

: Repay outstanding Facility B borrowings under the Senior Facilities Agreement, pay anticipated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the WINS Exchange and WOW Issuance, and use any remainder for general corporate purposes.
